bull_bear.body:
- Chennai Metro penetration executed at the right time, already contributing ~20% of total revenue on an annualised basis
- All retail outlets, including newly opened Chennai Metro outlets, are EBITDA positive and PBT positive even after Head Office amortization
- Consistent execution: five-year CAGR of ~40% in Revenue and ~74% in PAT, attributed to effective inventory/liquidity management and a cost-effective delivery model
- Growing non-gold segment contribution diversifying beyond gold price dependence
- Disciplined funding model of one-third equity, customer advances and bank borrowings for expansion
- Forward hedging via MCX and gold metal loan structures to manage gold price risk and protect margins
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Gold price fluctuation — Frequent up/down moves in gold prices could adversely impact earnings; company runs a centralised procurement policy, gold-on-lease from banks with daily purchases matched to sales, and maintains inventory price hedging on a ~96:04 basis to safeguard against price swings.
- Economic slowdown / discretionary demand — A slowdown can hit demand and sales for what is a discretionary consumer purchase; mitigated by a diversified product portfolio and the structural link of jewellery demand to weddings and traditional occasions, especially in Tamil Nadu (India's largest gold-consuming state).
- Competition — Rising competition from new entrants and existing players; countered through quality products, competitive pricing, and extensive promotion/advertising to build brand positioning and recall.
- Margin / cost control — Lack of control over costs can lower profitability and impair growth; managed via centralised bulk procurement when gold prices are low, economies of scale, and correct procurement timing to reduce raw-material cost.
- Change in government policies — New taxation and stringent banking norms can disrupt demand and the supply chain; company relies on experienced IT and managerial personnel to analyse implications and ensure compliance.
- Human resources / attrition — Employee attrition may affect operations; mitigated by encouraging new talent, specialised sales-force training, improved performance standards, and incentive schemes.
- Seasonality — Sluggish sales from seasonal changes may affect profitability; mitigated by a wide-ranging designed product profile aligned to customer needs across seasons.
- Compliance — Non-compliance with regulations raises operational risk; addressed through a structured internal control system covering statutory rules and changes in taxation and regulatory framework.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Thangamayil Jewellery Limited (TMJL) is an organised jewellery retailer selling gold, silver, diamond and non-gold jewellery through a network of company retail outlets, with recent growth concentrated in the Chennai Metro region alongside its established South India footprint. It runs a same-store-sales (SSS) retail model, exchanging old gold for new pieces and funding growth through a mix of equity, customer advances and bank borrowings. Management emphasises inventory/liquidity management, a cost-effective delivery model and gold-price hedging as core to the operating model.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- TMJL follows a balanced dividend philosophy that rewards shareholders while preserving capital adequacy, funding growth through a mix of balanced dividends and retained earnings. The stated intent is sustainable growth without overstretching capital, resilience against external shocks, and consistent shareholder value creation. The company pursues expansion via an asset-light model and applies a 'margin of safety' principle to risk management, aiming to maintain all outlets above EBITDA level and preserve capital adequacy while expanding.
- Ethical sourcing: maintains a supply chain sourcing collections from reputable, trusted jewellers and suppliers.
- In-store certified gold testing and carat-checking machinery to guarantee purity/transparency at point of sale.
- BRSR prepared per SEBI LODR Reg 34(2)(f); externally assured (Limited Assurance) by J. Sundharesan & Associates.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Thangamayil's expansion is centred on a multi-store retail rollout, anchored by its penetration of the Chennai Metro market. In FY25-26 the Company opened 10 new outlets, funded through its standing 1/3-1/3-1/3 rationale of equity infusion, customer advances and bank borrowings. The Chennai Division already contributes nearly 20% of total revenue on an annualised basis, and management expects this to rise to 25% by FY27-28 upon completion of the second phase of expansion. Under expansion phase-II, the Company plans to open at least nine outlets in FY26-27, with initial civil/interior works already underway; the entire phase-II is targeted for completion by 31/12/2026, and both capex and working-capital funding are already tied up. The Company has obtained working-capital sanctions from its member bankers of up to Rs.1,412 Crores, stated to be sufficient to complete expansion plan-II in the Chennai Metro and surrounding areas. Management notes all retail outlets, including the newly opened Chennai Metro stores, are EBITDA positive and PBT positive even after head-office amortization. Beyond store rollout, strategic thrusts include Tier 2/Tier 3 market expansion, omnichannel and digital capability build-out, product innovation and premiumisation (lightweight everyday-wear, men's and children's jewellery), high-value/studded and third-party branded diversification, and CRM/loyalty and gold-savings schemes.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural migration from the unorganised to the organised jewellery segment is accelerating, driven by mandatory BIS hallmarking, GST compliance, transparent pricing, and rising consumer preference for certified, branded jewellery.
- Indian wedding demand (industry estimated at USD 50+ billion) is the primary demand anchor, with bridal jewellery accounting for approximately half of gold jewellery consumption; a high volume of weddings in the November 2025 to March 2026 season supported demand despite elevated gold prices.
- High gold prices during FY 2025-26 are shifting consumers toward lighter-weight, lower-carat pieces, fashion jewellery, and affordable luxury, with younger buyers favouring versatile everyday pieces over pure occasion-led purchases.
- Demand for personalisation and customisation (initial pendants, zodiac charms, birthstone rings, engraved pieces) is accelerating sharply, with brands offering personalised jewellery reporting customer lifetime value up to 40% higher than standardised collections.
- Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities are emerging as the new growth frontier, with consumers there exhibiting the same brand aspiration and quality consciousness as metropolitan buyers.
- Digital and omnichannel adoption is deepening — e-commerce influences over 60% of metro purchase decisions and retailers with robust omnichannel strategies capture 30% larger consumer spending share than single-channel operators.
- During the FY 2025-26 gold-price rally (domestic prices up ~73%), India's gold jewellery demand by volume declined while value rose to an all-time high; large organised retailers weathered the environment better than smaller unbranded competitors, supported by higher ticket prices, wedding-season purchases, and brand trust.
- Rising affluence, income-tax rationalisation (Union Budget 2025-26), and up-trading (purchases above Rs 25,000 grew fastest in FY26) are expanding discretionary jewellery spending, with the discretionary retail segment projected to grow at a 10-12% CAGR through 2028.
- Women, constituting nearly 43% of India's online shoppers and an expanding share of the formal workforce, are reshaping purchase patterns toward lightweight everyday-wear jewellery alongside traditional occasion pieces.
- Favourable government policy — customs tariff on jewellery (HSN 7113) cut from 25% to 20%, platinum findings from 25% to 5%, GST maintained at 3%, AEO status extended to exporters, and continued mandatory hallmarking — supports formalisation and consumer trust.
- Sustainability and ethical sourcing (responsibly sourced materials, recycled gold, conflict-free diamonds, eco-friendly packaging, lab-grown diamonds as a sustainable alternative) are a growing influence on purchase behaviour among younger, urban demographics.
